about.title: San Jacinto Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a collision on State Street, Ramona Expressway, or San Jacinto Avenue takes a family member's life, the grief is only part of what's left behind. Riverside County families are often left facing funeral costs, lost income, and an empty space no settlement can truly fill. San Jacinto recorded 162 injury collisions and 3 traffic deaths in the most recent reporting year, with Wednesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing higher crash activity than other times. California law gives certain family members a limited window and a defined path to pursue a wrongful death claim against the at-fault party. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free service that connects grieving families with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened, explain your options, and handle the legal work while you focus on your family. There's no fee unless the claim results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What San Jacinto Families Should Know

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases, generally to a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in some situations. An attorney can help determine who in your family qualifies to bring the claim.

items.title: The Clock Starts Right Away
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity, like a public road authority, may share fault. Given how many of San Jacinto's collisions happen on public roadways, this distinction matters and is worth checking early.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond the Financial
items.desc: California law allows families to seek recovery for funeral and burial expenses and lost financial support, as well as the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. An attorney can help make sure all of these losses are properly accounted for, not just the immediate bills.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, a surviving spouse, registered domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none of those relatives exist, other dependents or heirs may be eligible under California law. An independent attorney can review your family's specific situation to clarify who qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a death in San Jacinto?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. That deadline can be much shorter if the crash may involve a government entity, such as a claim tied to a public roadway like Ramona Expressway. Because of how quickly this timeline can close, it helps to speak with someone as soon as you're able.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, they are separate matters. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil case brought by the family to recover their own losses. One can proceed regardless of the outcome of the other.
